observations:
Torah 262 is a short, tightly structured teaching with a single argument arc. After identifying all four packages (שֵׂכֶל/מַעְיָן, בְּכִי/מַסֶּכֶת, נְהָרוֹת, קְלִפּוֹת/סִטְרָא אָחֳרָא), every concept in the text has been accounted for:

1. הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הַתּוֹרָה (Torah innovation) — connected to Package 1 via eitza (produces the spring), not via bechina. It does not have three or more bechina partners in the text that would justify its own independent package. It is a single eitza-source node.

2. יְשִׁיבוֹת (academies) — mentioned once in passing with no bechina language, as a location where rivers form. Insufficient bechina language to form or join a package.

3. The river-metaphor terminology ('מַעְיָן' growing into 'נְהָרוֹת') does not constitute a second neutral package separate from the existing spring/intellect package — the spring is a bechina of the sekhel (Package 1), while the rivers are the downstream structural conduit (Package 3).

For a new package to be warranted, the source text would need three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language that form an independent domain not covered by the existing four packages. No such cluster exists in this five-sentence Torah. The existing four packages fully cover: (a) the good intellectual source (Package 1), (b) the good protective mechanism (Package 2), (c) the neutral structural conduit (Package 3), and (d) the evil opposition (Package 4). The Torah's structure is complete.
